text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The agricultural ministry may raise milk prices, which could hurt the country's dairy exports.
- People suspected of criminal activities and their families will have to prove that their income and property was acquired legally under a law passed by parliament on Thursday.
- The social insurance and pension fund deficit in the first half of 1997 was almost 200 million litas.
- Lithuanian Airlines may acquire a Boeing 767 and launch transatlantic flights.

- No high ranking politicians or banking officials attended the funeral of the president of Tauras Bank, Genadijus Konopliovas, who was found dead with a bullet wound to his head on Monday. Police suspect he committed suicide.
- The Bank of Lithuania is expected to decide on the fate of Tauras Bank next week. Preliminary data shows that the bank is insolvent.
- Parliament decided to impose sticter penalties for money laundering crimes.
- The government decided to ask for parliament's approval to issue a state guarantee to six western banks for a $101.58 million credit for the construction of the Butinge oil terminal.

- The government decided to reorganise the Lithuanian Energy firm and to pass the heating branch to 16 municipalities. Lithuanian Energy will remain the biggest firm in the country with share capital of 1.8 billion litas.
